main_issue: Whether to keep the leaving colleague's chosen Korean barbecue (which D can't attend) or switch to a single alternative restaurant all four can go to.

A-B.evidence: A first offered a no-beef compromise (7) and B stressed her favourite place (9); then A accepted changing (13, 21) and B kept objecting (14, 22, 24).

A-C.evidence: A first defended the booking and C's timing (4); then A agreed to change (13) and 'one place it is' (21), matching C's view (15, 19).

A-D.evidence: A offered no beef (7) and D declined (8); then A: 'We'll have to change it' (13), and asked for suggestions (21), matching D's (26).

B-C.evidence: C suggested another place (10) and B opposed (14, 16). C rejected the split plan (17, 19); C challenged B's reasoning (23, 25).

B-D.evidence: B pushed for the original place and a split plan (16); D rejected it ('simpler to stick to one place', 20) and asked for another place (26).

C-D.evidence: C proposed another place (10) and D agreed (11); D 'I agree with Agent C' (20); both keep to one place together (23, 26).
